_doc: Metal printing in a powder bed (direct metal laser sintering, DMLS, or laser powder bed fusion), from a printing service's design guide: a part optimised for it has the problem's overhang ('+z') and no enclosed voids, since powder left inside can't be got out (topopt voids finds them). The optimiser holds overhangs at 45 degrees, which this set's 45 matches; 316L stainless asks 55, which it does not model. kind community: a service's published guidance; your printer's figures beat it.
name: dmls

overhang.rule: Faces held up by themselves at no less than this from the build plate

bridge.rule: The longest span left unsupported (0.080 in.); longer, the faces underneath come out poor

hole_min.rule: Holes smaller than this (0.025 in.) tend to seal shut or come out small

feature_min.rule: The smallest solid feature at normal resolution (0.012 in.)
feature_min.source: Protolabs, design tip: 7 mistakes to avoid when designing 3D printed parts, https://protolabs.com/resources/design-tips/7-mistakes-to-avoid-when-designing-3d-printed-parts

escape_hole.rule: A hollow needs a hole at least this wide (2 to 5 mm are used) to let its powder out, on a face nobody sees
